literal: Wife (acc.) he who fears, will fear indeed always, to good people good things to do.
translation: He who fears his wife will always be afraid to do good deeds for good people.
modern: தன் மனைவிக்கு அஞ்சுகின்றவன், நல்லவர்களுக்கு நல்ல செயல்களைச் செய்வதற்கும் எப்போதும் அஞ்சுவான்.
explanation: This couplet explains that a man who is overly afraid of his wife will lack the courage to perform virtuous deeds. 'இல்லாளை அஞ்சுவான்' refers to a husband who lives in constant fear of his wife's displeasure. Because his actions are entirely dictated by this fear, he 'அஞ்சும்' (will fear) to do 'நல்ல' (good things) for 'நல்லார்க்கு' (good people) at all times ('எஞ்ஞான்றும்'). Thus, his submissiveness prevents him from fulfilling his moral and social duties.
